findings.desc: CHK-002 userSees pins a literal tamper message that is itself the stale-enumeration defect this story removes, and the implementer correctly REFUSED to ship it. The pinned text names the signed fields as "(agentResults/issues/background/title/description/checklist were modified)" - a hand-written enumeration that goes wrong the next time the domain changes. What shipped instead renders the domain from its single declaration (INIT_CHECK_SIGNATURE_DOMAIN), which is what plan.md DoneWhen and the dispatch both asked for. AUTHOR OF THE DEFECT: the main agent, when writing the acceptance field in PLAN. The implementer flagged the conflict and reported it rather than silently self-correcting or silently complying, which is the correct behaviour. userSees is frozen from DEV (checklist_update refuses it by design, so the executor cannot move the acceptance goalposts) - this finding is the sanctioned channel for recording that the pinned criterion was superseded. RESOLUTION SOUGHT: accept the rendered message as satisfying CHK-002 acceptance, on the record, rather than reopening PLAN to edit the field. The shipped behaviour is strictly better than the pinned text.

concept-cleanup: docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-agent-prompt-consolidation-execution-plan.md:839 still asserts the PRE-CHK-002 init-check.json signature domain as current fact — "`_hash` covers story background/title/description/checklist hash/reviewRound; high/critical issues block" — implying issues/agentResults are outside the signature, which B-8df9 CHK-002 falsified (INIT_CHECK_SIGNATURE_DOMAIN now covers agentResults+issues via computeInitCheckVerdictHash). This same file explicitly states its Artifact Schema table "records current code-backed contracts", so this is not historical narrative, it is a live factual claim now wrong. CHK-005/CHK-006 fixed the equivalent stale assertions in CLAUDE.md:538/544/580 and docs/requirements/decisions/story-lifecycle.md:73, but this decision doc (also inside the story scope contracts allowedModify wildcard docs/requirements/decisions/*.md) was left unfixed — a residual reference to the redefined concept.

concept-cleanup: computeInitCheckVerdictHash (packages/main/src/core/init-check-gate.ts:169-178) defines a NEW private module-scoped canonicalJson(value) — recursive key-sorted, undefined-dropping JSON canonicalization — duplicating logic that already exists as the exported canonicalJson in packages/main/src/core/digest.ts:36-38, whose own header comment says it was extracted into a leaf module specifically "so it can be reused without dragging handler dependencies along" (already reused by core/review-run.ts). init-check-gate.ts already imports nothing else from digest.ts, so nothing blocks reuse; the two implementations sort keys by different comparators (digest.ts: a.localeCompare(b); init-check-gate.ts: a<b?-1:a>b?1:0) and diverge on null-vs-array handling, so this is not a byte-identical duplicate — it is a second, subtly different canonicalization routine for a signature/hashing code path, which is exactly the kind of unintentional near-duplicate that should not survive introducing a new signed-hash helper.

doc-code-drift: docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-agent-prompt-consolidation-execution-plan.md:839 states in the current-code-backed-contracts table that init-check.json _hash "covers story background/title/description/checklist hash/reviewRound" only. That is now stale/incomplete: B-8df9 CHK-002 widened INIT_CHECK_SIGNATURE_DOMAIN (packages/main/src/core/init-check-gate.ts) to also cover the reviewer verdict (agentResults + issues, via computeInitCheckVerdictHash) so that a hand-edited verdict fails the signature. This is the second surviving instance of the pre-CHK-002 formula (the first, packages/main/src/handlers/init-preflight.ts:143, is a known/accepted survivor named in the story scope contract); this row in a decisions/*.md file was in this story's explicit allowedModify scope (docs/requirements/decisions/*.md) and was not updated. A reader consulting this plan for the proof-or-stop migration would inherit the wrong belief that the signature does not bind reviewer coverage, risking re-introduction of the exact defect B-8df9 fixed.

packages/main/src/handlers/init-preflight.ts:136-138 (initCheckRow) still open-codes the init-check _hash comparison (`const expectedHash = recomputeInitCheckHash(storyId, store, projectRoot); if (initCheck._hash !== expectedHash)`) instead of routing through the CHK-003 single trust predicate (initCheckHashMatches / initCheckSignatureIsValid) declared once in core/init-check-gate.ts precisely so no consumer re-invents this comparison. Two concrete consequences: (1) it performs a second independent store.readInitCheck read inside recomputeInitCheckHash rather than verifying the snapshot the caller already holds in `initCheck` -- the exact double-read/race pattern CHK-003 explicitly closed in machine.ts (module comment: verify against the SNAPSHOT already read, not a second read of the file). (2) initCheckHashMatches trims stored/expected hash strings and treats blank as untrusted, while the raw `!==` here does not, so a persisted _hash with incidental whitespace would be judged VALID by the real gate (canEnterInitCheckGuard / getGuardFailureReason, both correctly migrated to initCheckSignatureIsValid by this story) but reported [STALE] by this preflight row -- a live disagreement between the authoritative gate and its own preflight surveyor. Confirmed this is not caught by any existing test: init-preflight-smoke.ts assertAgreement() only asserts the aggregate report.gate.ready/blockedBy (which IS computed correctly via getGuardFailureReason at init-preflight.ts:287), never the individual init-check row status this function returns. Not touched by this diff, but directly falsifies the story-wide claim (repeated in init-check-gate.ts module doc and CLAUDE.md) that the trust predicate is declared once so it cannot silently diverge from what the gate uses -- this is exactly the remaining comparison site the story asked reviewers to rule out.

packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:645 (selectorMatched = run.output.includes(pinSelector), exact substring) means CHK-002:happy:0's pinned selector "GREEN: both verdict fields are inside the signature domain." (checklist.json, recorded 2026-08-01T15:18 against red-b8df9-init-check-verdict-signature.mjs) is now permanently unmatchable: CHK-003 legitimately extended the SAME artifact's final conclusion print (tests/red/red-b8df9-init-check-verdict-signature.mjs:665-671) to "GREEN: both verdict fields are inside the signature domain, and the carry-forward refuses to re-sign..." (comma, not period, after domain). Reconfirmed live by re-running node bin/lattice.js validate --focus=b8df9-init-check-signature just now: the exact pinned string does not appear in current output. Because VerificationIntentPin is immutable once set (core/types.ts:287-291) and this artifact is a PERMANENT lattice.config.json validate.commands regression check (the CHK-002 waiver was withdrawn), this must-priority happy-path evidence can never again be re-earned as literally recorded. verification_evidence_refresh_stale (handlers/checklist.ts:1833-1877) re-executes the pinned command on staleness; on selector mismatch it falls to the demote path (checklist.ts:906-926), silently converting a mechanical:true receipt into mechanical:false with an auto-generated "receipt invalidated" reason while leaving result:pass untouched. Not currently blocking REVIEW->TEST (recorded receipt is intact), but materialHash has moved since this evidence was recorded (init-check-gate.ts/store.ts/handlers/init-check.ts/command-policy.ts all changed afterward via CHK-003/005/006), so the next legitimate refresh -- e.g. done_prepare --refreshStale, which CLAUDE.md requires before DONE -- will trigger the demotion. This is exactly the class of durability defect the review task flagged (a selector anchored to a mutable summary sentence rather than a stable per-row claim id), the same class that produced a finding against predecessor story B-49d4.
